review_items.frank_statement: EffectIntent is a serializable proposal; an opaque host-minted permit and release-time revalidation enforce effects; no ambient OS authority is granted to model output.
review_items.counterhypothesis: A metadata-only capability contract, or a single Linux sandbox backend such as Landlock, is sufficient and no layered host enforcement design is needed.
review_items.falsifier: A required Frank v0.1 Ubuntu effect either cannot be securely represented/lowered with current CapabilityToken/EffectIntent plus typed host adapters, or a simpler single-backend design proves equivalent isolation, recovery, coverage and lower complexity across the complete Ubuntu effect suite.

independent_checks.source: Linux kernel Landlock userspace API documentation
independent_checks.result: Landlock explicitly targets restriction of ambient rights and is stackable, supporting the external-enforcement concept.
Ubuntu uses AppArmor as a default Linux Security Module confinement layer, supporting an Ubuntu-native outer enforcement option.

independent_checks.source: WebAssembly WASI capabilities and Component Model WIT resource-handle specifications
independent_checks.result: Independent capability-system design uses unforgeable runtime handles and owned/borrowed resource handles rather than textual authority.
Namespace/chroot/read-only resource injection enforced a narrow read capability; unsandboxed baseline retained ambient filesystem authority.

adversarial_checks.result: FAILED in current container with ENOSYS despite modern kernel surface; single-backend assumption rejected.
FAILED; ordinary unsandboxed process could read /etc/passwd and read/write test resource.
PASS; removing the resource bind denied the previously available resource.
PASS; read-only remount allowed read and denied write with EROFS.

review_items.reason: The external-authority boundary is independently supported, but its Ubuntu realization must not assume one sandbox API. The refined design is an opaque host capability table plus runtime-probed layered Linux enforcement and receipts.
review_items.claycode_action: Preserve current CapabilityToken/EffectIntent semantics. Specify Ubuntu lowering/runtime ABI so textual/model references never mint authority; host revalidates scope/revocation and maps only authorized resources/verbs into the sandbox. Treat AppArmor/Landlock/namespaces/seccomp as backend mechanisms, not ClayCode semantic authority.
